description: Create a tag automation rule. Appends one rule after the existing ones; existing rules are untouched. The rule fires on a newly filed item carrying any of `tags` (or whose type is in `types`) and applies its actions: `user` assigns a person, `connector` hands the item to a connected coding agent (launching…

agentPrompt.description: Steering prompt for the launched agent. Only kept alongside a `connector`.

connector.description: Connected coding agent to hand the item to — a connector id from `ops agents list`.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is live. Defaults to `true`.

listToken.description: REQUIRED. The `listToken` returned by the most recent `ops_routing_rules_list` call. It proves you listed existing ops routing rules and confirmed this one doesn't already exist before creating it. Call `ops_routing_rules_list` first if you don't have a fresh token.

priority.description: Triage priority of a queue item. The lowest tier is `nice_to_have` (not `low`) — carried over from the feature-request "importance" scale this priority set replaced.

skipApproval.description: Let a matching public-intake ticket skip `pending_approval`. Defaults to `false`.

status.description: Lifecycle status of a queue item. The working flow is `open` → `in_progress` → `ready_for_qa` → `resolved` (or `wont_fix`, terminal from any earlier stage). `blocked` marks an item that can't progress until an external dependency clears — a working state a human sets and clears. `ready_for_qa` is what a developer sets once a fix lands; `resolved` is the QA sign-off, normally flipped in the dashboard after verification — set it directly from code only when the fix has been verified end-to-end. `investigating_by_ai` is a system-owned display state — set when the AI agent (Jarvis) picks an item up to investigate, never chosen by a human — so it is shown but not offered as a manual choice. `pending_approval` is the one human-gated holding state: it parks an item OUT of the work queue until a human promotes it to `open` in the dashboard, so `GET /api/admin/ops` excludes it under `status=all`/default and returns it only when requested as an exact `status`. It covers untriaged inbound that must never be auto-implemented — connector requests filed from a customer's connectors panel, and questions funnelled in from the "Stuck in onboarding?" assistant — where approving means flipping the status to `open`. Two earlier values were removed in favour of this single gate: `triage` (the onboarding-help bucket, now `pending_approval`) and `triaged` (a redundant "looked at but not started" step, now plain `open`).

tags.description: Tag names the rule matches (case-insensitive). Tags are created on first use.

types.description: Ticket types the rule also fires on.

items.description: A ticket type a tag rule can also fire on. Error and alert tickets carry no tags, so a rule that should catch them matches on type.

user.description: Person to assign — a user id.

name: ops_routing_rules_create
